Class Abilities

1st Level

Fast Movement

  • Effect: Monk moves at the rate shown in the table above. Being over the carrying limit removes Fast Movement and reduces this to 30ft.
  • Sure Climber: you roll Climb with Dexterity.

Iron Body

  • Effect: Advantage on saves against poison, disease, paralysis, petrification and death effects.

Ki

  • Effect: You have ki points equal to your Monk level + your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). You regain them all after a long rest.
  • Stun Attack (the default): declare before the attack roll; on a hit, spend 1 ki and the target makes a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC or is Stunned for 1 round (1d4 rounds from 10th level).
  • A miss costs nothing.
  • Once per round; your first stun attempt must be a primary attack.
  • Deals normal unarmed damage.

Parrying Stance

  • Effect: While unarmed and unarmoured, once per round when struck in melee, add your Wisdom modifier to your AC against that single attack, applied after the attacker rolls.

Hand-to-Hand Combat

  • Effect: See the table above for unarmed damage by level.
  • Your unarmed attacks use Strength or Dexterity (your choice).
  • From 3rd level, when you use your action to attack you make a second unarmed blow (the Secondary column).
  • Your blows never have the Disadvantage of an extra attack: they are rolled normally, are not off-hand attacks, and stack with Flowing Strikes and Haste.
  • A Monk never gains Extra Attack.
  • One target: until 9th level (Flowing Flurry), all your blows in a turn go at the same creature.
  • The monk has Advantage on all overbearing and grappling attacks
  • The monk may choose whether a successful strike deals normal damage or non-lethal damage

2nd Level

Deflect (Dexterity)

  • Effect: Out of turn, when a nonmagical missile would hit you (not a siege weapon), make a Dexterity check (d20 + Dexterity modifier) against the attack roll; on a success it does no damage.
  • Attempts per round: the table above.
  • You need a free hand, and can't deflect while surprised or Incapacitated.
  • 5th level: a melee attack too
  • 7th level: on a success against a melee attack, you may hold the weapon instead (the attacker takes it back with a Strength contest)
  • 10th level: a magical missile too, such as an enchanted arrow or a spell that makes a ranged attack roll

3rd Level

Iron Fists

  • Effect: Your unarmed attacks count as magic weapons, so they can harm creatures that only magic weapons can hurt. From 7th level they gain +1 to hit and damage, +2 from 13th and +3 from 19th.

4th Level

Slow Fall

  • Effect: Halve falling damage; from 10th level, you take none from a fall of 40ft or less.

Weapon Mastery

  • Effect: Choose one monk weapon: Stun Attack, Deflect and Death Strike work through it as if you were unarmed, and it uses your unarmed damage if that is higher.

5th Level

Flurry of Blows

  • Effect: When you use your action to attack, you make a third unarmed blow (Secondary column damage), at the same creature as your other blows. If two of them hit it, it is pushed 10ft or knocked Prone (your choice; a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC stops the Prone).
  • 13th level: a fourth blow (the Tertiary column)

6th Level

Ascetic Recovery

  • Effect: Feign Death: slow vital functions until appearing dead. Maintain the state for minutes equal to character level.
  • Fast Healing: after a long rest you regain 1 HP per Monk level on top of the usual.

8th Level

Iron Mind

  • Effect: Advantage on saves against charm, fear, confusion and other mind-affecting effects.

9th Level

  • Ki: Body of Iron: at the start of your turn, spend 2 ki to end one condition affecting you (stunned, paralysed, poisoned, frightened, charmed, etc.). It costs no action and works even while incapacitated.

Flowing Flurry

  • Effect: You may move between your blows, and aim each at a different creature.

10th Level

Ki: Death Strike

  • Effect: Declare before the attack roll. The target's Level must be no more than half your Monk level. On a hit that deals damage, spend 4 ki: the target must make a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC or die instantly.
  • A 12th level monk may delay the death — the target dies at any point the monk chooses within rounds equal to monk's level, or the monk can release the sentence with a successful touch attack instead
  • The death strike has no effect on undead, oozes, elementals, or creatures that magic weapons cannot harm

13th Level

  • Untouchable: The first attack that would hit you each encounter is a Deflect that succeeds without a roll. Does not work against attacks the Monk cannot perceive (invisible, surprise, etc.).

15th Level

  • Wisdom Bonus: permanent +1 Wisdom. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation).

18th Level

  • Flowing Form: your unarmed attacks count as having the Reach and Entangling traits.

20th Level

  • Body of Iron Made Whole: when you spend ki on Body of Iron, it removes all conditions currently affecting you and heals 4d8 HP.

Renown: Monastery

  • Effect: You may found a monastery (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 1d6 novices and one 1st-level Monk join it. While you hold it, a full day's meditation there restores all your ki and removes one level of Exhaustion.

24th Level

  • Untouchable improves: up to a number of hits each encounter equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) miss instead, no more than one each round.

Feats of Arneyan

The Monk may choose from the Martial Path at any Feat level without needing to multiclass.

Kits: Monastic Traditions

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Monk folder. Drag one onto your character.

Monk Kits represent the tradition, school, or circumstance that shaped the character's training. The peoples, orders and places a kit names are examples, not the only ones: a kit suits anyone from a tradition like it.
